purpose: Acalabrutinib is used to treat certain types of blood cancers, including chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL), and mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). It helps slow down or stop the growth of cancer cells. Your doctor chose this medicine because it targets cancer cells more specifically than traditional chemotherapy.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have a protein called BTK (Bruton's tyrosine kinase) that helps them grow and survive. Acalabrutinib works like a lock-and-key — it blocks that protein so the cancer cells can no longer get the signal they need to multiply. Without that signal, the cancer cells stop growing and eventually die off.
common_side_effects: Headache (especially in the first few weeks), feeling tired or weak, diarrhea, bruising more easily than usual, muscle or joint pain, nausea, and upper respiratory infections like a common cold. Headaches often get better over time and can be helped by drinking plenty of water and taking acetaminophen (Tylenol).
warnings: This medicine can increase your risk of serious bleeding, so let your doctor know before any surgery or dental work. It can also raise your risk of infections, irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation), and in rare cases other cancers. Avoid grapefruit and do not take antacids like Tums at the same time — take them 2 hours apart. Do not use proton pump inhibitors like omeprazole regularly while on this drug. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 100 mg taken by mouth twice a day, about 12 hours apart. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush or open them. Try to take it at the same times every day to keep steady levels in your body.
